newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot natgas prices rise above index levels.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot natgas prices rise above index levels.

text.p: Despite expectations for cooler weather later this week, U.S. spot natural gas prices jumped more than 10 cents over index levels Tuesday as storage buying continued at a fairly steady pace, industry sources said.
Gulf Coast gas traded in the mid-$1.80s to mid-$1.90s, with the weaker prices evident in late trading.
At the Henry Hub, La., prices hovered in the low-to-mid $1.90s.
"We're not going in where we were last year," said one trader, referring to storage inventories. "People should be trying to put as much as they can into storage."
The trader added that a daily increase of two to three billion cubic feet (bcf) over the historical injection rate would be needed to reach year-ago storage levels.
Early injection estimates for Wednesday's American Gas Association report still ranged from 63 to 80 bcf.
The strength in Gulf prices filtered into the Appalachian market where most deals were reported done about five cents higher in the $2.11-2.16 area.
In the Midcontinent, prices inched up more than five cents over indices into the high-$1.70s to low-$1.80s, with Demarcation quoted at the high end of the range.

Despite the moderating demand in the Gulf and Midcontinent markets, buyers on the West Coast were out in larger numbers today as Canadian exports were scarce because of the cold temperatures in the province.
As a result, Permian basin prices jumped more than 10 cents into the low-to-mid $1.80s.
